accounting.rationale: 6.1.5 p1, PDF 67, printed 53, line 27 identifies the special-character class through Table 6.1. The heading is at line 26. Membership is not permission to use each character as a stand-alone lexical token. The Fortran-character-set union stays in 6.1.1 p2 and default-character support stays in 7.4.4.2 p3 (PDF 84). No additional semantic S ID is allocated.

PDF 68, printed 54: all 32 entries in the 16 visual rows are subdivided in row order, left then right. Each entry defines a member; none duplicates the graphic obligation owned by S6.1.1-001. That owner's four processor source/display-interface facets remain pending. Its currency exception and unspecified graphic style apply to this table. No encoding, numeric code, font, or mandatory dollar glyph is inferred.

Left entry, row 1: the blank is a special-character member even though its graphic cell has no visible ink. This is not an ASCII-code-32 oracle or a mandate for a particular space width. Its source-form uses are separately specified in 6.3.2.2 and 6.3.3.1.
Right entry, row 1: semicolon membership; token classification and statement termination remain in 6.2.1, 6.3.2.5, and 6.3.3.4.
Left entry, row 2: equals membership; this does not reclassify assignment as a defined operator or change the separate equals token in 6.2.1.
Right entry, row 2: exclamation-point membership; comment initiation and its character-context and fixed-column exceptions stay in 6.3.2.3 and 6.3.3.2.
Left entry, row 3: plus membership, not a new arithmetic or sign rule.
Right entry, row 3: quotation-mark membership, also named quote. Literal and edit-string delimiter rules remain in R724 and R1322.
Left entry, row 4: minus membership, not a new arithmetic or sign rule.
Right entry, row 4: percent membership; its independent token and component-selector contexts remain canonical.
Left entry, row 5: asterisk membership; multiplication, kind/length notation, commentary, and I/O uses are not newly specified here.
Right entry, row 5: ampersand membership; continuation and character-context behavior remain source-form rules.
Left entry, row 6: slash membership; operator, delimiter, and editing contexts retain their defining rules.
Right entry, row 6: tilde membership. Inclusion does not invent a tilde operator or independently legal statement token.
Left entry, row 7: backslash membership. Inclusion supplies no escape-sequence semantics or permission to change ordinary literal interpretation.
Right entry, row 7: less-than membership; relational syntax and semantics remain in Clause 10.
Left entry, row 8: left-parenthesis membership; 6.2.6 and enclosing syntax retain delimiter ownership.
Right entry, row 8: greater-than membership; relational syntax and semantics remain in Clause 10.
Left entry, row 9: right-parenthesis membership; matching and enclosing grammar are not new effects here.
Right entry, row 9: question-mark membership; 6.2.1 owns its token alternative and the conditional-expression and conditional-argument rules own its valid contexts.
Left entry, row 10: left-square-bracket membership, without duplicating delimiter or enclosing construct rules.
Right entry, row 10: apostrophe membership. Its printed typographic style is not a requirement to encode source with a particular Unicode code point. R724 and R1322 retain the delimiter rules.
Left entry, row 11: right-square-bracket membership, without duplicating delimiter or enclosing construct rules.
Right entry, row 11: grave-accent membership. No additional operator, name character, or stand-alone token is inferred.
Left entry, row 12: left-curly-bracket membership. The table is not permission to add a brace-delimited language construct.
Right entry, row 12: circumflex-accent membership. This does not define exponentiation or a bitwise operator with this spelling.
Left entry, row 13: right-curly-bracket membership. The table is not permission to add a brace-delimited language construct.
Right entry, row 13: vertical-line membership; no logical or bitwise token is invented.
Left entry, row 14: comma membership; list separators and its separate lexical-token classification remain canonical.

Right entry, row 14: currency-symbol membership. The graphic exception in 6.1.1 p3 is retained under S6.1.1-001: the displayed dollar-like example is not a mandatory dollar glyph, ASCII value, source byte, or runtime identity oracle.
Left entry, row 15: one member with the decimal-point and period names. Literal and dotted-token rules remain in their defining sections.
Right entry, row 15: number-sign membership. A preprocessing directive is not inferred to be standard Fortran syntax.
Left entry, row 16: colon membership. Single-colon and double-colon token alternatives and their enclosing contexts retain separate ownership.
Right entry, row 16: commercial-at membership. Membership does not extend R603's name grammar or introduce another lexical token.

PDF 68, printed 54, lines 1-2 describes four kinds of use of some table members. This is neither an exhaustive assignment of functions to the 32 members nor a new executable requirement. Subdivide the uses while leaving their defining syntax and effects in place.
The operator-use description points to existing spelling and operation rules in 6.2.4 and Clause 10; it does not declare every special character an operator.
The bracketing-use description does not expand 6.2.6's delimiter list or the enclosing grammar.
The separating-use description does not replace the source-form or token-separation rules with a new mandatory effect.
The delimiting-use description refers to particular canonical contexts, including literal and edit-string delimiters; it is not an independent context-free admission or rejection oracle.
